reviews.text:
The veterinary nurses are all so kind and wonderful.
My French Bulldog is prone to heatstroke, but they not only keep him cool and provide cooling during the examination, but they also let me drive him out before I paid... I'm truly grateful.

They are always so kind and helpful.

My dog ​​hates having his temperature taken (he really dislikes having the thermometer inserted into his rump), but they explain it to him carefully, and when the nurse holds him firmly, he becomes very cooperative. They also listen carefully to what I have to say about my dog, and I think they are a great vet.

When I was examined by the head doctor, I was very satisfied with his polite and reassuring treatment.

However, when I was examined by other doctors, I got the impression that they were somewhat cold, and I felt that they were not able to respond flexibly to my needs.

I also felt that there was a difference in the level of care provided by the nurses.

I believe that the choice of words and the way one interacts with patients are very important.

I plan to use a different hospital in the future.

My beloved cat took me to the hospital many times because he was not feeling well.
I repeatedly told him that he seemed to be having difficulty walking, was listless, and had lost his appetite, but he was simply told he was fine and prescribed only a nutritious diet.

Still worried, I took him to another hospital, where he was diagnosed with pneumonia and well-advanced FIP.
His condition then rapidly worsened, and he passed away.

I still wonder if the outcome might have been different if I had received appropriate tests and more detailed explanations sooner.
I would only take my child there if it was absolutely necessary. It might be okay if the doctor wasn't a woman. After reading the reviews, I agree.

This is an extremely cold and inhumane hospital that shows no compassion for animals.

The other day, my beloved dog fell off a chair, had a seizure, and was in critical condition. I immediately called this hospital, which I had visited before, and then hurriedly hailed a taxi and arrived. It was 6:03 PM, three minutes past closing time, so they said they couldn't see him. No matter how much I pleaded, explaining that it was a life-or-death situation and asking if they could at least take a look, they were completely unyielding. The veterinarian showed no intention of coming out to check on him, and the receptionist simply refused.

Therefore, we had no choice but to quickly find another emergency hospital. It was quite a difficult experience for both us and our dog.

I will never go to such a cold animal hospital again!

After getting the rabies vaccine,
he started to walk with a limp when we got home.
He didn't get better even after a few days, so we took him to two other hospitals, but they said that maybe the vaccine was given too close to the muscle, causing it to stiffen and become unable to walk.
After watching for about two weeks, he finally got better,
but I was worried.
This was the first time something like this had happened, so I don't want to go again if possible.

I use this clinic occasionally, and the wait time is short. There's also a coin-operated parking lot nearby.

My dog ​​doesn't even seem to notice he's getting an injection; they're very skilled at giving injections and taking temperatures.
There was a parking lot and the staff were kind and helpful! Thank you very much!

I've trusted this veterinary clinic for the past four years. I'd always held it in high regard, but unfortunately, this experience has completely changed my opinion.

Today, I saw a veterinarian named Sakairi Hiko for the first time. She was overbearing, and whenever I asked, she would respond with a firm, "So, what do you want to do?", which made me feel uneasy. Her gaze was somewhat intimidating, and it didn't create an atmosphere where I could consult with her comfortably. I was forced to ask for a different veterinarian, but she made a gesture as if to violently throw the thermometer at me, which surprised me.

After that, they planned to switch to a different veterinarian, but the nurse told me it would take more than three hours for the next veterinarian to become available, so I was told to come back tomorrow. I was worried about my dog's condition, so I went there as an emergency, but I didn't receive adequate treatment, which left me feeling confused and disappointed.

I later learned that Sakairi Hiko had previously run her own clinic, but it had been unsuccessful and closed. Considering how she handled this situation, I can understand why.

This experience was truly disappointing, as I trusted this hospital. I wanted it to be a place where I could trust my pet's health, but I think I'll consider choosing a different hospital in the future.
I travel an hour each way to see the vet because he always puts the animals first.

The reception and examination were both very polite and excellent!

It's also great that you can get an examination even on weekends without prior reservation!

There is a parking lot, but it's a multi-story parking garage, so it seems you need to go to the reception when you arrive in front of the hospital and apply to use it before you can park.

There are vehicle size restrictions:
Length: 5,300mm
Width: 1,950mm
Height: 2,000mm
Weight: 2,300kg

Please be aware of these restrictions.

My previous cat-only veterinary clinic closed down, so I've been going to this one since this year.

It seems like they see a lot of dogs, but they also treat cats very carefully.

I walk there, but there's a multi-story parking garage, so it's convenient for those who drive.

The fees are reasonable.
You will receive excellent and courteous service.

The reception staff is absolutely terrible. Even an AI-powered free-form announcement system would be better. Their responses are barely answers to questions, and they just seem to be reading something monotonously, which is incredibly frustrating. I don't understand why they spend so much time asking for details when no appointment is necessary, and they keep asking about my current health condition even though they don't know when I'll be coming in.
